public_rationale: The March announcement establishes $122 billion in committed capital. Later reporting describes a proposed bridge round targeting at least $30 billion. That is relevant counterevidence to a claim about every individual request, but it does not establish a smaller annual financing requirement. No completed-year counterexample or other decisive event was established by October 28.
limitations: Funding need and fundraising totals are different measures.
The bridge-round report relies on unnamed sources and describes preliminary discussions.
No finite run of increasing requirements can establish every future year.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI will need more than it last asked for, without fail, every single year.

statement.excerpt: While various different venture capitalist paypigs may have some interest in funding it further, OpenAI will need more than it last asked for, without fail, every single year.

from_speaker: OpenAI will need more than it last asked for
our_interpretation: The plain reading is a claim about increasing annual external financing requirements, not merely larger company valuations.
The preceding $122 billion round supplies context for the initial comparison, but a completed round is not necessarily identical to the amount originally requested.
Calendar years are an evaluator convention; the speaker did not specify calendar versus fiscal years.
Need must be established from cash requirements. A smaller individual round does not establish a smaller full-year requirement.
No final year is stated, so this has an open horizon.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable records establish that each completed subsequent year's financing requirement exceeds the relevant preceding funding request. A finite sequence can support only those years, not the unrestricted every-year claim.
criteria.contradiction_condition: One completed subsequent year has a verified external financing requirement no greater than the preceding funding request.
